text:
Jamie Drysdale is playing 23 minutes a night, the most of his career, on a Flyers blue line that needs someone to move the puck. He has 10 points in 22 games, nine of them in his last ten, including three assists against Utah, and he and old Anaheim teammate Trevor Zegras are back together in Philadelphia.

The scoring is fair. One goal on two expected and a normal amount of on-ice luck: no bounces propping it up. The harder number is the play. The Flyers take only 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, four and a half points worse than without him, and he starts a lot of shifts in his own end.

His skating is the tool. NHL Edge has his top speed in the 94th percentile and his bursts over 20 mph in the 96th. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 38% of his entries last season, and Evolving-Hockey gave him most of his modest value on defense. He's 24. The minutes are a vote of confidence; the five-on-five results still have to catch up.
